holder_baseline.how_to_read: If the holder's own prior transactions are confirmed fraud, this holder identity is compromised: matching its baseline is evidence FOR fraud, not against it. A holder is defined by card, billing region and anchor day, so its history is always in its own region: whether the region is new can only be read at card level (alert_context.card_history.flagged_region_share_of_card).

shared_origin.how_to_read: lift = share of transactions on this element scoring >= 0.5, divided by the same share across all transactions. Large regions and common email domains carry many unrelated cards; a shared origin needs lift well above 1 and several distinct cards.

assessment.reasoning: Alert HHF-015 was triggered by a legacy real-time risk score on transaction 3601725 ($112.75). Analysis of the knowledge graph indicates this alert is a false alarm. Transaction 3601725 was conducted in person for product W in region 485. While the card was predominantly active in region 325 in January 2017, region 485 is not new: card C00543-K1 has 9 prior transactions in region 485 (7.8% of historical card transactions), including several in-person product W purchases of nearly identical amounts (~$108 in transactions 3238041, 3301272, and 3390280). Furthermore, the cardholder's baseline and recent activity show unvarying adherence to in-person product W purchases, with no channel, product, or velocity shifts. There is no customer dispute. Community detection places the card in community 54526279 with zero fraud cases (lift 0.0), ring_id is -1, and regional activity in region 485 shows 0 high-scoring transactions across 188 events (lift 0.0). Similar closed cases CC-2956, CC-3616, CC-1266, and CC-0536 confirm that isolated model/risk alerts on in-person transactions in secondary cardholder regions represent legitimate cardholder activity. The transaction is legitimate.
